messages:
Elaine: quick sync: we need a minimal GA acceptance checklist that covers SLA language, pricing guardrails, runbooks for failover, and a public-facing rollback FAQ. aim to keep it small but legally and operationally actionable.
Priya: +1. For SLA language I suggest baseline: 99.5% global uptime for self-serve, 99.9% for paid tiers. include credits formula: (downtime_minutes / monthly_minutes) * invoice, cap at 50%. Also require reported incidents within 24h window.
Marco: ops note: our current autoscale cold-starts mean worst-case p95 latency could spike for long sequences. that needs to be explicit in docs and the SLA should exclude cold-start windows and force-migrate customers to Dedicated if they need hard low-latency.
Tasha: pricing: we need a capped burst metric on the public page. propose examples: "standard" includes 200 requests/min burst with 2x throttling; "enterprise" negotiable. also document cost predictability path -> Dedicated discounts and prediction docs.
Elaine: legal: do we want a data residency opt-in checkbox for Private deployments and a short paragraph about customer-controlled keys?
Priya: yes. short clause: "Customer may elect data residency and KMS options; Redwood will provide deployment boundaries and an addendum." keeps it lightweight.
Marco: runbook checklist items: detection, notify (customers + oncall), failover to fallback model, enable read-only mode for console, start mitigation playbook. We should include exact CLI commands and Console toggles.
Tasha: also a customer-facing rollback FAQ with steps: how we notify, expected timeline, credits, and contact path. customers want predictability not legalese.
ops-bot: monitoring alert: latency p95 for /v1/chat crossing threshold in eu-central-1 at 2025-02-11T09:12Z.
Priya: monitoring SLOs: error budget per-region, token-rate anomaly detection, and smoke check every deployment. add a public dashboard link for enterprise customers.
Marco: technical escape-hatch: routing policy example to include immediate fallback to quantized model + cached prefix routing. sample: 
Marco: ```
route: /v1/chat/completions
routing_policy: "priority=fallback, fallback_model=redwood-small-quant, cache_prefix=enabled, throttle=2000/min"
```
Elaine: assigns: Marco -> add runbook commands + CLI snippets (24h); Priya -> draft SLA paragraph + credit calc (48h); Tasha -> pricing page sample + burst rules (48h). I'll create the GA acceptance checklist after those land.
Tasha: I'll add a clear migration path blurb for customers to go from hosted to Dedicated (including sample throughput numbers and cost delta).
Priya: legal ask: want a one-paragraph indemnity note and a short opt-out for beta features. will draft.
Marco: ops caveat: we need an ops headcount plan for GA P0s. current oncall rota might not meet 15m ack target for every region. recommend ramp plan doc.
Elaine: decision: for GA we'll set operational targets: P0 ack < 20m (paid), incident update cadence 1h, RCA within 72h. We can tighten after Month 1 metrics.
ops-bot: deploy notice: GA candidate rollout started in us-east-1 at 2025-02-11T09:30Z (build b4c2). monitor health checks.
Priya: I'll push SLA draft to legal review and tag finance.
Tasha: pricing draft will include worked examples for 10M tokens and 100M tokens.
Marco: runbook draft will include a checklist and the exact command set to flip routing flags.
Elaine: thanks team. I'll follow up with a consolidated checklist doc and share in this channel. reconvene Friday if blockers. :white_check_mark:
